oneliner.t: Two-term Republican U.S. representative for Georgia's 10th District and co-owner of the family's Jackson-based Collins Trucking, who won the June 16, 2026 GOP runoff with Trump's endorsement to challenge Sen. Jon Ossoff.

upbringing.t: Michael Allen Collins Jr. was born and raised in Jackson, Georgia, son of Mac Collins, a Republican congressman for eight terms (1993–2005) who lost a 2004 Senate bid. He graduated from Piedmont Academy in Monticello in 1985 and earned a business administration degree from Georgia State University in 1990. In the early 1990s he and his wife, Leigh Ann, started Collins Trucking in Jackson; trade press traces the family's hauling business to an earlier Collins concrete-pipe company. He later chaired the board of a large Georgia credit union and served as president of the local chamber of commerce. The couple have three children.

career.role: Co-founder/co-owner; his 2025 disclosure lists a 55% interest in Collins Family Enterprises, Inc. (operating as Collins Trucking Company) and a $28,600 salary
career.org: Collins Trucking Company / Collins Family Enterprises, Inc., Jackson, GA

career.role: Candidate, GA-10 (lost GOP runoff to Jody Hice)

platform.t: Runs as an 'America First' 'MAGA workhorse'; says he votes with the President 100% of the time and wants a Republican Congress to deliver Trump's agenda. Endorsed by Trump after the May primary.
Highlights the Laken Riley Act, which he authored (detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft); accuses Ossoff of weak border policy and of wanting to defund ICE and Border Patrol.
Defends Trump's tariffs as leveling the field with China and the 2025 tax cuts; blames inflation on Biden-era policy.
Blames the ACA for rising premiums and credits the 2025 law's rural-health program; says Ossoff wants a federal takeover of health care.
Backs the SAVE Act (proof of citizenship and photo ID to vote).
Says Trump 'had every right' to act to stop Iran getting a nuclear weapon.
Describes himself as '100 percent pro-life, period. No exceptions'; cosponsored a January 2025 fetal-personhood bill.

promises.t: Help President Trump deliver his America First agenda in the Senate.
Vote with the President 100% of the time.
Pass the SAVE Act's proof-of-citizenship and voter-ID requirements.
Prioritize immigration enforcement in the spirit of the Laken Riley Act.

record.t: Born July 2, 1967, in Jackson; born and raised there.

record.t: He and his wife started Collins Trucking in the early 1990s, when he would have been about 25. Trade press traces the business's roots to the family's earlier concrete-pipe company. The one-truck detail was not independently documented.

claims.claim: Passed two bills into law in his first two years, under two presidents: the TRANQ Act and the Laken Riley Act.

said.where: campaign About page; also Senate launch release (2025-07-28)

record.t: The Laken Riley Act (his bill) passed both chambers and was signed by President Trump in January 2025. His TRANQ Act (H.R. 1734) passed both chambers in December 2023 (Wikipedia). Its presidential signature was not confirmed in a source opened here, so the 'two presidents' half rests on that.

claims.claim: The Laken Riley Act was the first bill President Trump signed in his second term.

record.t: Signed by Trump in January 2025. Whether it was the first bill signed was not confirmed in a source opened during research.

claims.claim: Named chairman of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Subcommittee on Water Resources and Environment.

record.t: He sits on Transportation and Infrastructure (Wikipedia); Trucknews lists him on its Highways & Transit subcommittee. The chairmanship was not confirmed in an official source opened here.

claims.claim: Appointed to the House Whip Team.
Served as President of the Butts County Chamber of Commerce and chaired the board of Georgia's Associated Credit Union.

claims.claim: Chaired the board of the Georgia Motor Trucking Association.
Married to Leigh Ann; three children and six grandchildren.

said.t: Campaigns on immigration enforcement and the Laken Riley Act.

entries.t: Campaign ad in which he said 'Donald Trump won this state, period' and shot a voting machine; has repeatedly echoed claims that the 2020 election was rigged.
Called Jan. 6 participants 'peaceful protestors' who were treated unjustly.
Said government has liability when it harms people, in response to a Jan. 6 defendant; campaign says he opposes a blank-check payout fund.
Voted to show support for Israel after the Oct. 7 attacks; voted against military aid to Ukraine; supports arms sales to Taiwan; voted for a 2023 resolution to withdraw U.S. troops from Syria.

positions.topic: Public statements drawing criticism (his own posts)

entries.t: Feb. 2024: suggested a migrant (later found misidentified) get 'a ticket on Pinochet Air'; X account temporarily suspended. March 2024: amplified a post from an antisemitic account attacking a Jewish journalist, which he said was about her 'stolen land' remark.
May 2026: his campaign X account mocked a rival operative's wife, a Matt Lauer accuser. He called the post 'despicable and unauthorized' and fired chief of staff Brandon Phillips (May 22).

Aug. 2026: said his son-in-law 'has had no role in my campaign whatsoever' after reports on the son-in-law's own posts, and that he condemns antisemitism. The son-in-law's posts are not attributed to Collins.

note.t: 2025 annual report (filed Aug. 4, 2026): the main asset is a 55% interest in Collins Family Enterprises, Inc. (Collins Trucking), $5M–$25M, with $100K–$1M S-corp income. Other assets: 50% of Collins Land & Property LLC, which rents a building to the trucking company ($250K–$500K); a crypto account of $250K–$500K (Ethereum $100K–$250K, Aerodrome, Ski Mask Dog, SUI, The Graph); credit-union deposits; 401(k)s and IRAs. Liabilities: a mortgage and a HELOC with Associated Credit Union, a personally guaranteed Truist line of credit for Collins Trucking ($250K–$500K), and a demand note to Collins Family Enterprises ($250K–$500K). In 2025 he reported 19 purchases/sales, almost all crypto (Ethereum, Virtuals Protocol, the 'Ski Mask Dog' meme coin, The Graph, Sui, USDC), plus one spouse IRA fund purchase. He filed 18 periodic transaction reports, 2023–Jan. 2026. None of his committees (Natural Resources; Science, Space and Technology; Transportation and Infrastructure) has primary crypto jurisdiction, so no trade overlap is listed. Note, though, that he sits on Transportation and Infrastructure, which oversees trucking, while holding a majority stake in a trucking company (a holding, not a trade). PolitiFact rated True an Ossoff claim that Collins is one of Congress's most active crypto traders. The net-worth range is assets minus liabilities from the disclosure bands (crypto counted once at the account level; the guaranteed company credit line counted as a liability; personal residence not listed).

Called Jan. 6 participants 'peaceful protestors' treated 'unjustly' and Capitol visitors 'peaceful grandmothers.'
Told a pardoned Jan. 6 defendant the federal government has 'a liability' when it harms people; campaign later said he opposes a blank-check payout fund.

note.t: Born and raised in Jackson, Georgia (1967); attended school in Monticello and Atlanta (Georgia State), and his business, rental property and church (Milner) are all in the Jackson/Butts County area.

legal.t: The Office of Congressional Conduct (formerly OCE) referred a complaint to the House Ethics Committee on Oct. 7, 2025, and the committee announced its review in November 2025. The OCC report released in January 2026 found 'substantial reason to believe' Collins used official funds to pay chief of staff Brandon Phillips for unofficial or unauthorized work (possibly campaign work on government salary), and that Phillips's girlfriend was paid more than $5,000 as an intern while allegedly doing no work. Collins's lawyer asked for dismissal, saying she did work in 2023–24. After Collins fired Phillips on May 22, 2026, the committee lost jurisdiction over Phillips but continues to review Collins. No committee finding or sanction yet; the case could lapse when his House term ends in January 2027.
legal.short: OCC referral; House Ethics review open
legal.status: Pending before House Ethics Committee — OCC preliminary finding only; no committee finding, as of July 2026 reporting

corp.t: Business PAC money in every House cycle and the Senate race. In 2025–26, about $104,000 from corporate PACs (e.g., Home Depot, UPS, Koch Inc., Georgia Power, Coca-Cola, Delta, General Dynamics) and $93,000 from trade-association PACs (e.g., America's Credit Unions, auto dealers, concrete, beer wholesalers, trucking, realtors), per donor-side FEC records. The crypto-industry super PAC Fellowship PAC spent $1.05M for him in the primary.

lobby.t: AIPAC PAC gave $5,000 directly to his committee in the 2026 cycle. The U.S.-Cuba Democracy PAC gave $1,000 in the 2016 cycle (to his 2014 committee, which was carrying debt). No United Democracy Project spending found.

research_notes: FAMILY RECORD SEPARATED: Sophia's raw record merges FEC IDs H2GA03070 and S4GA11053, which belong to his father, Mac Collins (House 1993–2005; 2004 Senate race). Those cycles (2000–2010), and 'Mac Collins for Congress' transfers listed as top donors, are excluded here. Only H4GA10071 (his House committee, 2014–2026) and S6GA00390 (Senate) are used. The career PAC totals in the raw record ('pac', 'lob') include Mac Collins's money and should not be shown for this candidate; the 2026 'pac26' block is his. MONEY: 'other' ($2.45M) = receipts minus individuals, PACs and self, likely the transfer from his House committee (not itemized here). pac_biz = corporate $104,000 + trade $93,000 + labor $18,000; pac_ideo = leadership $217,000 + ideological $39,500 + membership $21,000 + super PAC/hybrid $19,500 + candidate committees $23,000 (donor-side; sums to $535K vs. $495,632 recipient-side). Debts of $461,915.72 are largely candidate loans carried from 2014 and 2022 ($175,000 + $531,000 loaned, less repayments). Q2-26 figure (about $2.1M) is from FOX 5/Augusta Press. Small/large split, industries, top individual donors, in-state share and super PAC donor lists (Fellowship PAC, No Going Back PAC) were not retrieved. Q3 report due Oct. 15 not included. NOT FOUND/NOT CHECKED: GovTrack missed votes; sponsored/enacted bill counts; whether the TRANQ Act was signed into law; T&I subcommittee chairmanship; Heritage score; AIPAC's endorsement page; Track AIPAC; caucus memberships; House roll calls on Israel (clerk.house.gov not reachable). STAFF: Wikipedia also reports prior criticism of Phillips's criminal record, of successor Kip Talley's presence in a group chat with white nationalists, and an Aug. 2026 Washington Post report that a former staffer posted Nazi/KKK imagery. These concern staff conduct, are not Collins's own acts, and were not independently opened. Son-in-law David Scheer's posts are his own record, not the candidate's. The 'Deliver' (Aug. 24, 2026) ad text could not be opened. Photo omitted (no confirmed file URL).
